samples.summary: The new `requestLayoutRefresh` seam (measure-without-paint during a held undo unit) has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: The diff adds `textEditor.requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:2531) and calls it from the render wrapper (text-editor.ts:739), justified by "the rest of the unit reads `getLayout()` — `blockParentMap` (the paste path branches on it) and wrap affinity". No test references `requestLayoutRefresh` at all (grep across the repo for `requestLayoutRefresh` in any *test* file: 0 hits), and none of the new tests exercises a mid-unit layout read: the frontend paint test only counts `ctx.save` (`editor-undo-selection.test.ts:362`), and the docs `withUndoUnit` cases are on plain paragraphs. So if the wiring were dropped or the wrapper stopped calling it, every suite would stay green while the paste/table path inside an open unit read a stale `blockParentMap` — i.e. wrote into the wrong cell/block. A test that pastes over a selection inside a table cell (or asserts the hook is invoked while a unit is open) is missing.
searchedFor: grep requestLayoutRefresh across repo (only src + design docs, no tests)

samples.summary: No test for the documented "held render is replayed even after a throw" behavior of withUndoUnit
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s doc comment claims interior renders are "held and replayed once — at most once — after the outermost unit commits, including after a throw, so the screen always shows what the store really holds" (text-editor.ts:3821-3828). The only render-related test is `editor-undo-selection.test.ts:362` ('paints once for the whole action'), which covers the success path; nothing throws inside a unit in any new or existing test, so a regression that leaves `renderAfterUndoUnit` set (screen permanently stale after a partially-applied action) would not be caught. Searched packages/docs/test and packages/frontend/tests for `withUndoUnit`/throw combinations — none.

samples.summary: Hangul commit that replaces a selection is newly one undo unit, with no test
samples.evidence: `applyHangulResult` now wraps `deleteSelection()` + `docInsertText()` in `withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts:5891). No test covers it: the docs IME tests run against the snapshot-based MemDocStore and explicitly note the "exactly one Yorkie undo unit" assertion does not live there (`packages/docs/test/view/ime-composition-editor.test.ts:19-21`), and grepping packages/frontend/tests for composition/hangul finds only `yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` (store-level, not the editor path). This is the same #1045 shape (delete N blocks then insert) so an undo-unit regression here loses the document tail, but the failure requires software-Hangul input, so scope is contained.
searchedFor: grep composition|hangul in packages/frontend/tests -> only yorkie-doc-store.test.ts

samples.summary: The programmatic `pasteContent`/`insertPlainText` path newly wrapped in withUndoUnit is untested for undo cost
samples.evidence: The diff wraps the programmatic text-insert path (text-editor.ts:831-843) in `withUndoUnit`, but the new undo-unit assertions all go through keyboard/clipboard events (typing, Cmd+V paste, Enter, Cmd+Enter, Cmd+Shift+V, Backspace) in `editor-undo-selection.test.ts`. I found no test invoking the programmatic API and counting undo units, so a regression there (delete + insert split into two units) ships silently.
searchedFor: grep withUndoUnit call sites in src and cross-checked each against tests

samples.summary: The two new Cmd+Shift+V guard tests have no positive control, so they would pass if the shortcut never fired
samples.evidence: Both new docs tests assert only absence of a write (`expect(text).not.toContain('PLAIN')` at :423 and `expect(text).toBe('seed')` at :450). Neither asserts that `readText()` was even called, and there is no test in packages/docs asserting that a Cmd+Shift+V *does* paste (grep for `readText` in packages/docs/test returns only this file). If the shortcut handling changed (key/modifier/guard ordering) so `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` never ran, both tests would stay green while claiming to cover the `disposed`/`pasting` re-validation added at text-editor.ts:4254 — i.e. fake coverage for a data-safety guard. A `readText` spy assertion, or a happy-path plain-paste case in the same file, would fix it.
searchedFor: frontend editor-undo-selection.test.ts:441-470 has the positive Cmd+Shift+V case, but in another package/host

samples.summary: Two of the new adoption tests do not discriminate the new behavior (they pass on the pre-change implementation)
samples.evidence: 'a batch that writes nothing keeps the checkpoint it adopted' (:339) and 'an adopted checkpoint survives a batch that writes nothing' (:467) both hold under the old code path too: previously `snapshot()` pushed a checkpoint and `batch()` pushed a second identical one which `wroteNothing` popped, leaving exactly one checkpoint — so `canUndo()` is `true`, one `undo()` restores 'Hello', and the trailing `deleteText` case behaves identically. Only 'snapshot() immediately before a batch is still one undo unit' (:317, via `expect(store.canUndo()).toBe(false)`) actually pins adoption. Worth an assertion that distinguishes the adopted-vs-pushed checkpoint (e.g. undo-stack depth / no second dead Cmd+Z) in the two cases that claim to cover it.
searchedFor: hand-simulated pre-diff batch() semantics for each new case

samples.summary: `willWrite()` was added to ~30 mutators; redo-clearing is only tested through insertText/deleteText
samples.evidence: The diff adds `this.willWrite()` to setDocument, replaceDocument, updateBlock, insertBlock(s)(After), deleteBlock(ByIndex), setPageSetup, setDocStyles, updateStyleDefinition, resetStyle, resetAllStyles, setHeader/Footer, all table ops, applyStyle, splitBlock, mergeBlocks, setBlockType, applyBlockStyle, cell style/span and insertImageInline. Every new redo test in memory.test.ts (:421-521) drives only `insertText`/`deleteText`/`applyStyle`, so a mutator that is missed on a future addition (or one whose `willWrite` is removed) would leave a stale redo entry that Cmd+Shift+Z applies over a diverged document — undetected. A table/style-path redo case would close the gap cheaply.
